findings.evidence: Phase 1 items 1-5 restate sections 1.2, 1.4, 1.5 and 1.6 ('The `--diagrams` and `--reuse-from` checks (1.2)... A promotion head is a head in `PR_PROMOTION_BRANCHES` that differs from the base'). Section 4 repeats the reviewer rule from Phase 3 item 5, and generic facts the model knows are spelled out ('`git checkout -b` on git older than 2.23', 'The command does not fail because a reviewer was rejected')
findings.fix: Keep each rule once. Make Phase 1 and Phase 3 short ordered pointers to the numbered sections ('1. Validate (1.2). 2. Head and guard (1.6)...'), and delete the generic git fallback and the repeated restatements of the reviewer outcome

findings.evidence: Rules are split between declarative sections (1.x, 2.x) and an ordered phase list that keeps pointing back ('(1.6)', '(2.7)', 'per 2.9'). At 386 lines this goes well past the ~200-line Process pattern
findings.fix: Make the six phases the spine. Put each rule inside the phase that runs it, and keep only definitions (1.3 diagram, 1.4 REPO, 1.5 PRD) as standalone sections, so the agent reads the steps in order and does not jump between sections

findings.evidence: 'never create `pr-diagrams/<N>` or `pr-diagrams-<N>` (phase 5)': the gotcha says what not to do but not why
findings.fix: Add the reason. For example: a per-PR branch name collides with the single `pr-diagrams` ref namespace (a branch `pr-diagrams` blocks `pr-diagrams/<N>`) and leaves orphan branches that `publish` never cleans up

findings.evidence: The command is 386 lines. The same plugin-root fallback paragraph ('read `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/...` first; when that text is unsubstituted ... read `$HOME/.claude/...` instead, testing it with `[[ -f ... ]]` rather than a quoted `~`') appears at lines 132, 212, 224, 299, 336 and 384. The long final-message ordering paragraph (line 254) and the 2.8 filter description also stay inline
findings.fix: Define the resolution rule once (for example 'Resolve <rel> = first existing of ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/<rel>, $HOME/.claude/<rel>') and cite it at each load point. Move the final-message ordering rules and the 2.8 filter prose into skills/pr-diagrams/references/pr-body.md, loaded on the failure or none-mode path

findings.evidence: 'Derive `<short-slug>` from the head name or the latest commit subject.' This gives two options and no default, and on this guard the head name is always the base (`main`)
findings.fix: Give one default: 'Derive `<short-slug>` from the latest commit subject (lowercase, hyphenated, at most 40 characters); fall back to `pr/<yyyymmdd-hhmm>` when the subject is empty.'

findings.evidence: 'phases 1, 2, and 3 run in one Bash call that ends by writing `$AD/state.env`'. Phase 3 still needs agent judgment between reads: choosing SRC by `base_ref`, the merge-commit check in 2.2 ('stop before any PR write and ask the user'), and the mode decision from the 2.1 view. A single non-interactive Bash call cannot pause for those, so the branch has no clear outcome
findings.fix: Allow several Bash calls in phase 3. Write `$AD/state.env` progressively (append each value with `printf '%q'` as soon as it is known), and have every call after the first source it, so judgment steps can run between reads

findings.evidence: The feature and consolidated templates, the assembly code and the none-mode filter live only in pr-body.md ('read `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/...pr-body.md` first; ... read `$HOME/.claude/...pr-body.md` instead'). No outcome is given when both candidates are missing, unlike the Mermaid rules, which have stated minimums. The same gap exists for draw-io/SKILL.md at line 299
findings.fix: Add the missing branch: 'When neither pr-body.md exists, stop before any PR write with `pr-body.md not found at <both paths>` (phase 6 cleanup runs)'. For draw-io/SKILL.md, treat a missing file as a render failure (Mermaid fallback, warning first)
